interpretation: The refreshed screen separates input completeness, valuation, business quality and ownership of a gas bottleneck. NFE has the highest original Sweet Spot score, but negative EBITDA makes it an input exception; its valid annual FCF/EV is negative, not evidence of cheapness. LBRT and EXE lead among names with complete required fields. LBRT is a services/power business, so that result is a research prompt rather than confirmation of pipeline economics. All three-factor scores remain provisional because the TTF beta sample is historical.

Recent issuer releases provide a different layer of evidence. KMI reported Q3 adjusted EBITDA growth of 9% and a $13.2bn natural-gas project backlog; WMB reported 6% adjusted EBITDA growth. Cheniere raised 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $8.75-9.25bn. These support examination of operating infrastructure and delivery capacity, while current valuation still matters. ET's latest issuer results are available, but Yahoo EV/cash inputs are incomplete, so its missing valuation ratios are not supplied by guesswork.

NEXT remains a construction/start-up exposure: its October 29 update expects first Train 1 LNG in Q2 2027. EQT and RRC also carry a newly announced merger dependency, with completion expected in Q1 2027 subject to approvals. Producer gas-price exposure, LNG contract/marketing economics and fee-based pipeline activity require separate theses; the gross international-gas spread is not net realizable equity cash flow.

score_input_validity.headline_rule: Highest original score among current rows with all required finite fields. This is input completeness, not financial-quality approval; all TTF-based scores remain provisional.
score_input_validity.original_missingness_treatment: Raw invalid/missing ratios remain n/a. The unchanged scoring formula replaces missing factor z-score contributions with neutral zero; it does not impute raw prices, EV, EBITDA or capex. Missing-component scores are retained for transparency but excluded from the complete-input headline.
score_input_validity.ratio_sign_rules: EV and EBITDA must be positive for EV/EBITDA; EV must be positive for annual FCF/EV. Negative annual FCF is a valid negative yield, not cheapness. Net cash may produce a valid negative net-debt ratio with positive EBITDA.
